questions.stem: In thermal equilibrium, which quantity must be spatially constant throughout a connected semiconductor?
questions.explain: The Fermi level is flat in equilibrium. Carrier numbers can still change with doping.
questions.hint: The Fermi level is flat in equilibrium. Carrier numbers can still change with doping.

questions.stem: For an intrinsic semiconductor at equilibrium, which relation holds?
questions.explain: Intrinsic means electrons and holes are equal, both equal to n_i.
questions.hint: Intrinsic means electrons and holes are equal, both equal to n_i.

questions.stem: Acceptor-doped silicon (complete ionization, N_A >> n_i) is normally
choices: n-type with holes as minority carriers
p-type with holes as majority carriers
questions.explain: Acceptors make holes the majority carriers, so the sample is p-type.
questions.hint: Acceptors make holes the majority carriers, so the sample is p-type.

questions.stem: Electron drift velocity is directed
questions.explain: Electrons are negative, so they drift opposite the electric field E.
questions.hint: Electrons are negative, so they drift opposite the electric field E.

questions.stem: The Einstein relation connects
questions.explain: Einstein link: D = μ * V_T. Mobility and diffusivity stay tied together.
questions.hint: Einstein link: D = μ * V_T. Mobility and diffusivity stay tied together.

questions.stem: At 300 K, n-type Si has n = 2e16 cm^-3 and μ_n = 1000 cm^2/Vs. Calculate conductivity σ = q * n * μ (q=1.6e-19 C).
questions.hint: Use σ = q * n * μ with q = 1.6e-19, n = 2e16, μ = 1000. Compute 1.6e-19 * 2e16 first, then multiply by 1000. Enter an integer coefficient and the power of 10 (for example 259 and -4 for 0.0259).

questions.stem: Two mobility limits are 800 and 400 cm^2/Vs. Using Matthiessen (1/μ = 1/μ_1 + 1/μ_2), calculate μ.
questions.hint: Matthiessen: 1/μ = 1/800 + 1/400. Add those two terms on the calculator, then take the reciprocal 1/(...). Enter an integer coefficient and power of 10 (usually 0 here).

questions.stem: The mass-action law in a nondegenerate semiconductor at equilibrium is
questions.explain: In equilibrium, the product n p equals n_i squared.
questions.hint: In equilibrium, the product n p equals n_i squared.

questions.stem: For μ_n = 1000 cm^2/Vs at 300 K, calculate D_n = μ_n * V_T with V_T=0.0259 V.
questions.hint: Use D_n = μ_n * V_T with μ_n = 1000 and V_T = 0.0259. Multiply those two numbers. Enter an integer coefficient and the power of 10 (for example 259 and -4 for 0.0259).

questions.stem: N_c (effective density of states) varies approximately as
questions.explain: N_c grows like T to the power 3/2.
questions.hint: N_c grows like T to the power 3/2.

questions.stem: N_D = 6e15 cm^-3, N_A = 1e15 cm^-3, n_i negligible. Calculate majority electron concentration n_0 ≈ N_D − N_A.
questions.hint: Majority electrons: n_0 ≈ N_D - N_A with N_D = 6e15 and N_A = 1e15. Subtract, then enter coefficient and power of 10.

questions.stem: The Hall voltage sign is mainly useful for identifying
questions.explain: Hall polarity tells you if majority carriers are electrons or holes.
questions.hint: Hall polarity tells you if majority carriers are electrons or holes.

questions.stem: A donor atom in silicon becomes, after ionization,
choices: a fixed positive ion plus a mobile electron
a fixed negative ion plus a hole
electrically neutral with a mobile hole
questions.explain: The donor ion stays fixed; one electron is free to move.
questions.hint: The donor ion stays fixed; one electron is free to move.

questions.stem: Matthiessen’s rule combines scattering mechanisms by adding
questions.explain: You add 1/μ terms, not the mobilities themselves.
questions.hint: You add 1/μ terms, not the mobilities themselves.

questions.stem: The intrinsic carrier concentration decreases most strongly when
questions.explain: Larger E_g makes n_i drop very fast through the exp(−E_g/2kT) factor.
questions.hint: Larger E_g makes n_i drop very fast through the exp(−E_g/2kT) factor.

questions.stem: E = 100 V/cm and μ_n = 800 cm^2/Vs. Calculate electron drift speed magnitude v = μ * E.
questions.hint: Use v = μ * E with μ = 800 and E = 100. Multiply, then enter an integer coefficient and the power of 10.

questions.stem: In a graded n-type semiconductor at equilibrium, the built-in field primarily balances
questions.explain: Diffusion and drift currents cancel in equilibrium.
questions.hint: Diffusion and drift currents cancel in equilibrium.

questions.stem: Resistivity ρ relates to conductivity σ by
questions.explain: Resistivity is simply the inverse of conductivity.
questions.hint: Resistivity is simply the inverse of conductivity.

questions.stem: At 300 K, calculate V_T = k * T / q (standard room-temperature value ≈ 0.0259 V).
questions.explain: At room temperature, V_T is about 0.0259 V.
questions.hint: V_T = k * T / q at 300 K. Use ≈ 0.0259 V: enter coefficient and power of 10 (for example 259 and -4).

questions.stem: Majority carriers in strongly n-type material are
questions.explain: n-type means electrons are the majority carriers.
questions.hint: n-type means electrons are the majority carriers.

questions.stem: Complete ionization means dopant atoms have
questions.explain: Each dopant has given (or taken) its carrier, so N_D^+ ≈ N_D.
questions.hint: Each dopant has given (or taken) its carrier, so N_D^+ ≈ N_D.

questions.stem: Hole drift current points
choices: along the hole velocity / along E
questions.explain: Holes are positive, so their drift current follows E.
questions.hint: Holes are positive, so their drift current follows E.
